state.frozen_policy_content:
Gentle AI native bounded review policy.

Only candidate-caused BLOCKER or CRITICAL findings may require correction. Pre-existing and base-only findings are follow-ups. One correction is bounded by the frozen original scope. Gates are informational and unmanaged; ordinary repository policy decides delivery.
state.lens_selection_reason: adds a doctor check, an advisory warn status in the --json contract and a read-only Engram eligibility port (risk: contract and reads; resilience: unreadable pages or Engram; reliability: tests and goldens)

evidence: The change adds a read-only advisory doctor check (promoted-pages-eligible). It reads promoted pages and live Engram observations through existing adapters and writes nothing.
Its status is warn or PASS and never FAIL, so the doctor exit code cannot change. cmd_doctor.go still counts only CheckFailed, and the cmd tests cover this.

Output contains only page addresses, observation ids and topic_keys. The topic_key is quoted with %q, and the same data is already reachable through the tool's other commands. No secrets, injection, or authorization boundary is touched.

PageObservationID rejects ids of 0 or less, so a page is never joined to an observation it does not name. Pages whose observation is not live (deleted or in another project) are skipped, so no cross-project data is exposed.
No dependency or lockfile changes. The generated golden files were not available as content hunks; their metadata is consistent with an added trailing check line.
The new promoted-pages-eligible check never returns FAIL (it returns PASS or warn), and doctorExitCode counts only CheckFailed, so a warning cannot change the exit code or abort other checks.

Failure handling degrades gracefully: when the page list, the Engram read, or a port is unwired, the check returns a warn with the cause rather than erroring. Unwired or nil ports are guarded, including the nil eligibility function case.

Load is bounded: observations are read once per doctor run and only when at least one promoted page names an observation. This adds one extra Engram open of the same kind that embedding-index-fresh already performs, which is a negligible cost for a diagnostic command.
liveObservationIDs was refactored onto the shared liveObservations helper, which opens and closes the store with defer, so no handle leaks, and the ID semantics are unchanged.
Retry safety is not a concern because the check is read-only and idempotent.

Golden-file changes add a PASS line for the new check; the one warn golden (syncstate-golden 14, a vault root that is a file) is consistent with the check's cannot-judge path, and the exit codes are unchanged.

findings.claim: loadPromotedPages' per-page read errors are discarded, so an unreadable page is silently left out of the advisory check. The page checks report it, so this is acceptable. A unit test of this exists (TestDoctorLeavesAnUnreadablePageToThePageChecks), so no coverage gap.

evidence: Reviewed the full patch. The new advisory check is wired as the ninth check and answers PASS or warn, never FAIL. The exit-code logic counts only FAIL, and tests assert this at the command level for a warning alone, a warning beside a failure, and the JSON status.

Failure paths are covered: unwired reader, unreadable Engram database, unlistable pages, nil page reader and typed-nil page reader. Frozen pages, live-observation filtering and the eligibility rule are tested against promote.Eligible directly.
IneligibleReason calls Eligible itself, so the reason text stays in step with the rule. PageObservationID rejects id 0, and a test covers it.

The golden files for existing scenarios gained one line each at the end. Goldens 14 of syncstate and 13 and 49 of ops show a warn line for an unlistable pages directory; I could only read the syncstate one, since the ops goldens are summary-only.
I found no regression in baseline behavior and no BLOCKER or CRITICAL issue.
